summary.headline: The July split between oil and gas has closed: crude, European gas and power are now all rising together as attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz became more frequent through October. Brent is back at $107.89/barrel (+68.7% YoY), TTF gas is +169% YoY with EU storage at about 75% of capacity, the lowest since at least 2009, and the European electricity index is +114.5% YoY. Freight is the one pillar giving something back: ocean container rates are easing as Red Sea transits resume, though still more than double a year ago, while road freight keeps climbing on diesel. Labour is steady and legislated, but it is no longer ahead of headline inflation: euro-area HICP accelerated to 3.8% in September on energy.

pillars.commentary: Every energy series rose again, and the annual comparisons are now extreme: Brent +68.7% YoY, German diesel +61%, Ghent marine gasoil +106%, US Gulf jet fuel +110%. September's crude rally ran on supply fears after the US and Iran failed to reach a deal, and October extended it as tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz became more frequent while pipelines in Saudi Arabia and the UAE could not compensate. Europe's gas and power are the sharper problem for processors: TTF reached €85.92/MWh (+14.0% MoM) and the European electricity index €178.97/MWh (+12.3% MoM), with lower solar output and EU gas storage near 75% heading into winter. German baseload power averaged €162.95/MWh in September (+89% YoY). For food and beverage processing — drying, chilling, sterilising — this is the input that bites hardest, and market participants see no immediate end to the conflict.

pillars.commentary: Ocean freight has turned: the 40ft global composite index fell 2.6% MoM to about $4,351/unit in the first week of October, and Shanghai-Rotterdam dropped 10.3% MoM to about $3,337/unit as easing demand and more Red Sea transits pulled Asia-Europe rates down. But the annual comparison is still severe — the composite is +154% YoY and Shanghai-Rotterdam +99% — and backlogs at Far East ports, plus elevated Transpacific rates (Shanghai to New York about $10,320/unit), mean the fall may be slow. Road is the stickier problem: the European road freight index is +10.7% YoY, driven by diesel, with carriers under severe cash-flow pressure, some passing costs on through surcharges, and Black Sea disruption pushing more grain onto trucks. Air freight firmed +5.3% MoM after China's Golden Week.

drivers.name: Ocean container, US East Coast to North Europe

pillars.commentary: Labour is the pillar that does not correct, but it has stopped accelerating. EU manufacturing labour costs rose 2.9% YoY in Q2 2026, down from 3.3% in Q1, accommodation and food services 3.2%, and UK food manufacturing earnings 4.2% YoY in July. Because energy has lifted euro-area headline inflation to 3.8%, labour now trails the all-items rate by 0.9pp — in July it led by 0.5pp. Against food prices the picture is the opposite: euro-area food, alcohol and tobacco inflation is only 1.3%, and Expana notes that manufacturers are struggling to recover wage costs through product pricing. The pressure is policy-driven rather than a labour shortage: unemployment is stable at 6.1% in the EU, about 4% in Germany and 8.2% in France, and the UK Real Living Wage rose 6.75% in May.

drivers.name: Labour cost, manufacturing
drivers.note: Not seasonally adjusted — the quarterly rise reflects the usual seasonal pattern in the unadjusted series, not an acceleration in wage costs.

actions.label: Lock in energy pass-through rules before winter
actions.body: Gas and power are rising into the heating season: TTF +14.0% MoM and +168.9% YoY, the European electricity index +12.3% MoM, and EU gas storage near 75% of capacity, the lowest since at least 2009. Suppliers on energy-linked clauses will pass this through. Ask for the indexation formula and the reference month, apply it to the energy share of cost only, and do not accept surcharges anchored to a peak that has since moved.

actions.label: Book Asia-Europe volume while rates ease, and price road separately
actions.body: Ocean rates are falling (composite -2.6% MoM, Shanghai-Rotterdam -10.3% MoM) as Red Sea transits increase, which makes this a booking window for Q4 volumes — but both indices are still well above year-ago levels and port backlogs could slow the decline. Road freight is a separate story: with German diesel at €2.53/L and carriers under cash-flow strain, expect fuel-surcharge requests; tie them to a published diesel index and a base price.

actions.label: Index only the labour share of any wage-driven price request
actions.body: Wage pressure is policy-mandated, not a shortage of workers: the UK Real Living Wage rose 6.75% in May, and EU manufacturing labour costs are growing 2.9% YoY, slower than headline inflation but faster than food prices. In labour-heavy scopes such as packing, handling and catering services, ask for the labour share of cost in any repricing request and index only that share, rather than accepting a blended increase.
